title: Partition Control & Bounded Replay Orchestrator for Live Console Telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During tenant rebalances and autoscaler events we see prolonged downstream catch-up windows that either (a) drop tail events or (b) cause unbounded retry storms that breach latency SLOs for the Console. Objective: Build a lightweight coordinator that controls partition lease transitions and enables bounded, ordered replay for affected partitions so processors can resume to a known safe offset without spiking CPU or violating ordering guarantees. This ticket covers design, prototype, and staged rollout of the orchestrator service and small processor SDK changes.
success_criteria: 1) Partition rebalances complete with < 30s additional tail latency for affected tenants under steady traffic; 2) No duplicate metric emit counts in dashboards for a single tenant after a controlled replay; 3) On failure during replay, system gracefully pauses and exposes a replay cursor to the operator UI; 4) End-to-end tests simulating rebalance complete in CI.
approach:
- Introduce 'partition-control' coordinator service that manages lease handoff windows and issues bounded replay tokens.
- Processors will accept a replay token and use it to fetch a deterministic suffix from the durable append log (S3/KS) with explicit start/end offsets.
- Implement idempotent write semantics via dedupe keys for aggregation stages so replays are safe.
- Use a soft-quiesce period where producers continue to append but processors hold leases until replay completes or TTL expires.
- Expose control surface in Console: show partition state, replay progress, and allow manual abort/force-commit.
- Start with a canary rollout on a single non-critical region and a small tenant cohort.
risks:
- Risk of prolonged stall if replay log read is slow (mitigation: parallel prefetch and incremental checkpoints).
- Potential cost increase for storing short-term append logs (mitigation: short TTL and lifecycle policies).
- Complexity in cross-region coordination when leases move (mitigation: shard leader locality preference and fallback to last-known offsets).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token issuance and replay TTL enforcement.
- Integration tests: synthetic producer -> coordinator -> processor flow with induced failover.
- Chaos tests: kill coordinator mid-replay and validate processors pause and recover.
- Load test: replay a 10m event suffix for 50 tenants in staging and validate latency and CPU profiles.
- Regression test: verify no duplicate metric counts in historical dashboards after replay.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0: feature flag disabled; deploy coordinator and processor SDK changes to staging.
- Stage 1: enable for 1% of tenants in non-prod region behind feature flag. Monitor CPU, latency, dashboard delta.
- Stage 2: increase to 25% tenants and run extended load tests.
- Stage 3: enable globally with UI controls enabled and run a 48-hour observation window before GA.
- Rollback: disable feature flag and rely on existing lease semantics if we observe regressions.
monitoring:
- Dashboards: per-tenant replay duration, partition-state histogram, coordinator error rate, replay read latency.
- Alerts: coordinator replay-failure rate > 0.5% for 5m, or average replay duration > 120s for any tenant.
- SLOs: maintain 99th percentile console-metric-ingest end-to-end latency target for hosted tier.
- Audit logs: record replay token issuance and operator actions for compliance.

notes: Implementation will reuse the existing durable append API used by console-aggregator to avoid building a new persistence layer.
Follow-up work may include auto-compaction of short-lived replay segments and an operator API to export replay traces for postmortems.
Estimate assumes we can reuse the SDK idempotency facilities; if not, add 3 points to cover dedupe index work.
